new_statements.quote: Westlich des Logone, zwischen Bongor/Yagoua und Pala, betreten wir das Verbreitungsgebiet der Masa- und Zime-Sprachen einschließlich Mesme, Marba und Monogoy. Hier hat der Ton bereits die absolute Vorherrschaft übernommen. Um den vermehrten Funktionen angemessen entsprechen zu können, ist nun die Zahl der Tonebenen von zwei auf drei erhöht worden. [...] Abgesehen von jenen Überresten aus der Zeit alter segmentaler Morphologie herrscht im Zime wie im Masa allein der Ton als aspektdifferenzierendes Instrument. Im Dialekt von Batna zerfallen die Verben in zwei Klassen, die eine markiert durch Hoch gegen Tief (I), die andere (II) durch Hoch gegen Mittel.
new_statements.translation: West of the Logone, between Bongor/Yagoua and Pala, we enter the area of the Masa and Zime languages including Mesme, Marba and Monogoy. Here tone has already taken over absolute predominance. To meet the increased functions adequately, the number of tone levels has been raised from two to three. [...] Apart from those remnants of old segmental morphology, in Zime as in Masa tone alone serves as the aspect-differentiating device. In the Batna dialect the verbs fall into two classes, one marked by High vs Low (I), the other (II) by High vs Mid.
new_statements.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann. 2024. Emergenz und Genese der Tonalität im Tschadischen: Ein Beitrag zur Sprachgeschichte Nordostafrikas. Folia Orientalia 61: 167-192. DOI 10.24425/for.2024.152390.
new_statements.locator: p. 174-175 (opening of sect. 3) and p. 175 (before the Batna verb-class table); flip-flop statement p. 178
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: statement check: group-level-statement. Mirror the text: the three-tone-level claim is made for the 'Masa- und Zime-Sprachen' area and 'im Zime wie im Masa'; the verb-class detail is for 'Dialekt von Batna', which the article itself glosses 'Peve (von Batna)' = Peve [lme], and Dari examples are also Peve. Glottolog lists Kado/Zime among Ngete's alternative names, so Ngete sits inside Jungraithmayr's Zime cluster (Herde, Sorga, Dabrang, Tchimiang, Peve), but no tone statement is tied to an identifiably Ngete variety. | checker: File on mirror (kaba1292/ +, 1173 lines); title page shows FOLIA ORIENTALIA 61 (2024), DOI 10.24425/for.2024.152390, author Jungraithmayr; open publisher PDF; histori…
new_statements.relation_note: Zime (with Masa) is fully tonal, three tone levels; verbal aspect (perfective vs imperfective) is distinguished by tone alone (H vs L or H vs M by verb class); western (Herde) and eastern (Pala-Houa) dialects have reversed ('flip-flop') tone patterns; nothing on stress.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Zime (incl. the Ngete varieties Dabrang, Sorga, Tchimiang) is a tone language with three tone levels; tone alone marks verbal aspect (perfective H vs imperfective L or M); eastern vs western dialects show mirror-image tone patterns. No word-stress statement.
new_statements.exceptions: a few eastern dialects (Tchimiang, Dabrang) keep sporadic segmental (ablaut/suffix -a) aspect marking beside tone; devoicing of initial voiced consonants in the imperfective in western dialects (Batna, Dari, Herde)
new_statements.identity_note: Jungraithmayr's 'Zime' is the whole Zime/Kaɗo dialect cluster around Pala (Mayo-Kebbi), which ISO/Glottolog split into Ngete [nnn], Herdé [hed] and Pévé [lme]; Sorga and Dabrang, named here as Zime dialects and exemplified ('Zime von Dabrang', 'Tchimiang'), are Ngete villages/varieties (Ngete alt names Sorga-Ngete, Dabrang); the Batna (= Peve) and Herde examples belong to the sister lects. Statement is cluster-level and explicitly includes the Ngete varieties. [name in source: Zime (Dialekte: Herde, Sorga, Dabrang, Tchimiang, Peve von Batna; 'Zime von Dabrang', Pala-Houa; alter Name Kaɗo); pages 174-179 (sect. 3 'Im Zentrum: Masa und Zime'; Exkurs 2 'Père Court und der Flip-Flop')]

tone_statements.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann. 2024. Emergenz und Genese der Tonalität im Tschadischen: Ein Beitrag zur Sprachgeschichte Nordostafrikas. Folia Orientalia 61: 167-192. DOI 10.24425/for.2024.152390.
tone_statements.quote: Westlich des Logone, zwischen Bongor/Yagoua und Pala, betreten wir das Verbreitungsgebiet der Masa- und Zime-Sprachen einschließlich Mesme, Marba und Monogoy. Hier hat der Ton bereits die absolute Vorherrschaft übernommen. Um den vermehrten Funktionen angemessen entsprechen zu können, ist nun die Zahl der Tonebenen von zwei auf drei erhöht worden. [...] Wichtig ist nun, dass der Perfektivstamm durch einen hohen Ton, der Imperfektivstamm dagegen durch einen Mittelton markiert wird. Abgesehen von jenen Überresten aus der Zeit alter segmentaler Morphologie herrscht im Zime wie im Masa allein der Ton als aspektdifferenzierendes Instrument.
tone_statements.translation: West of the Logone, between Bongor/Yagoua and Pala, we enter the area of the Masa and Zime languages including Mesme, Marba and Monogoy. Here tone has already taken over absolute predominance. To serve its increased functions adequately, the number of tone levels has now been raised from two to three. [...] What matters now is that the perfective stem is marked by a high tone, the imperfective stem by a mid tone. Apart from those remnants from the time of old segmental morphology, in Zime as in Masa tone alone rules as the aspect-differentiating instrument.
tone_statements.locator: sect. 3 'Im Zentrum: Masa und Zime', pp. 174-175 (first part) and p. 175 after the Dabrang table (second part); flip-flop: Exkurs 2, pp. 177-178

tone.says: Masa-Zime languages are fully tonal: tone has 'absolute predominance' and the number of tone levels has been raised from two to three; verbal aspect is distinguished by tone alone (Dabrang: perfective stem High, imperfective Mid; Batna: class I H vs L, class II H vs M); only a few eastern Zime dialects (Tchimiang -a suffix, Dabrang i/a stem vowels) keep segmental remnants; Exkurs 2 (pp. 177-178): the Zime dialects fall into two tonological groups in a 'flip-flop' relation - West (e.g. Herde) pe…

sources.citation: [Vincent (site author, former cooperant at Pala) & Pierre Court (Mission Catholique de Pala, author of Lexique zime-francais, vun hed'e, 1984)]. 2000-2015. 'Site du dialecte Hede' (zime.free.fr): Le lexique zime-francais, vun hede (3533 entrees, 17 avril 2000) with the introductory notes 'L'alphabet du hede' and 'Les tons en vun hede' (signed 'Pierre'), plus 'Introduction au groupe linguistique Zime (Kado) dans le sud-ouest du Tchad' (intro.htm) and 'Quelques remarques' (remarques.htm). Website, last revised 2 August 2015.
sources.note: Three level tones (L marked grave, M unmarked, H marked acute) with a minimal triplet on 'su'; tone placement 'important pour marquer l'aspect verbal'; no mention of stress/accent anywhere on the site (intro, apprentissage, remarques, lexique pages searched for ton/accent/hauteur/intonation). Applies to Herde of Pala, a sister dialect; for Ngete it is at most cluster-level support, not a statement about nnn.
